regime_context: Rotation breadth is broad (73% of themes eligible), the gate has historically helped control drawdown on this market (gate_helps=true), and momentum leadership is bifurcated: one strong metals/semiconductor leader (Memory/HBM) with a fading durability bar, while a durable precious-metals block (Silver/Gold miners, trend-tagged, full breadth) sits just behind. Detector momentum is a focus lens only; the trust-graded truth is drawdown avoidance, not return forecasting.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Silver Miners (SIL) sustainably overtakes Memory/HBM (SMH) in relative leadership: if SIL's 20-day relative strength vs SMH turns positive and holds for 10 consecutive sessions while SMH's durability bar stays below 0.50, the precious-metals complex would be confirming a leadership handoff from the AI/semiconductor memory trade — retire this watch if SMH regains its 20-day high first.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners (GDX) shows the strongest combination of eligibility, trend-health ('trend' hurst), full breadth (1.0), and high durability-bar (0.84) with no crowding flag (z=0.55). Unlike the leader Memory/HBM whose durability bar is weak (0.44) and breadth is zero, Gold Miners' constructive trend discipline is the one validated leg, and the theme is not attention-saturated. This is a trend-following/vol-aware lean, not a momentum-rank buy.
theses.dissent: Gold miners have high beta to real yields and the dollar; if macro surprises push yields higher and the dollar rips, the trend can snap regardless of internal breadth. The rank #3 score also lags silver, so it may simply be a slower echo of a silver-led move.

falsifier.text: GDX closes more than 8% below its trailing 20-day high before the check-by date (30 trading days out).

theses.subject: Silver Miners
theses.thesis: Silver Miners (SIL) rank #2 with a strong durability-bar (0.79), full breadth (1.0), no crowding (z=0.69), and a sizable score gap over everything below it. It sits inside the same precious-metals complex as Gold Miners, so the constructive read is shared, but silver's extra industrial-demand beta makes it more volatile and less purely defensible than gold.
theses.dissent: Silver has a history of sharper drawdowns than gold on risk-off reversals, and the 'mixed' hurst tag means the trend is less mechanically clean than gold's. A broad commodity unwind would hit silver harder.

falsifier.text: SIL underperforms GDX by more than 5% over the next 30 trading days.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: Memory/HBM is the rank leader (score 3.05) but its durability-bar is weak (0.44), breadth is zero (0.0), and the headline reads 'fading'. The detector's one validated edge is avoiding shake-outs; a leader with zero breadth and a low durability bar is exactly the kind of momentum that can reverse hard. This is a de-risk/avoid lean, not a fade or short (the guardrails forbid fading the leader on reflexivity grounds).
theses.dissent: Single-stock/single-theme momentum can persist long past what breadth suggests; HBM has a real supply-demand story that may re-accelerate on an AI capex headline. Avoiding it forfeits upside if the fading flag is premature.

falsifier.text: SMH closes above its prior 20-day high with two consecutive closes above it before the check-by date (21 trading days out).
